channel.title: How We Got Here
channel.description: Ordinary people, extraordinary times - what it was really like to live through history's biggest moments. From gods and empires to trenches and technology: each episode opens with a broad era overview, then zooms into one individual's day - a Cullman farm boy in 1917, a flapper in 1920s Chicago, a Roman soldier in Judea - as history happens around them. Only verifiable history; dramatized scenes are labeled as reconstruction.

How We Got Here: The Baker's Wife of Paris
item.description:

item.title: How We Got Here: The Soldier at the Cross
item.description:
33 AD. Cassian is a Syrian auxiliary in the Roman cohort garrisoned at Jerusalem's Antonia Fortress, and this Passover Friday he draws execution detail at Golgotha. Walt opens up wide on the machine that made that morning - Tiberius's empire, Pilate's politics, a province holding a match - then zooms into one soldier's day, and asks the question that drives the whole episode: how did this happen?

item.title: How We Got Here: One Night in Chicago, 1926
item.description:
One Saturday night in a Chicago speakeasy, October 1926. A flapper, a bootlegger, and a suffragist's daughter walk into the same illegal room — and into the hinge of Prohibition, jazz, and the modern American woman. Standalone episode.

item.title: How We Got Here: The Gravedigger of Florence
item.description:
1348. Marco is a Florentine gravedigger, and this plague summer his parish churchyard fills, then the mass trenches begin. Walt opens up wide on the connected world that carried the plague - the Mongol roads, the Genoese galleys, the rats in the grain - then zooms into one working man's days, and asks the question that drives the whole episode: how did this happen?
